answer: Unrepeatable answer seeding: each identity must solve a fresh challenge whose correct response is derived from the prior one, so copying yields nothing. A new identity enters at the network's current difficulty nadir, forcing it to recompute the whole chain before acting. Like tending a garden, honest agents reuse verified work while attackers must regrow every link from seed. Sybils thus pay full recomputation cost in compute per identity, and any shortcut leaves timber unfit to build on.
